newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Sino/US summit promise good for HK stocks - analyst.
newsitem.headline: Sino/US summit promise good for HK stocks - analyst.

text.p: The promise of Sino/U.S. summits added to the positive background for the Hong Kong stock market, although it was not a fresh buy signal by itself, Howard Gorges, director at South China Brokerage, said on Sunday.

"The summit meetings are a good thing," Gorges said. "The market is not much affected by these sorts of things unless they really are negative, but it's been on the cards that Clinton and Jiang might meet and confirmation is certainly a plus factor."

U.S. President Bill Clinton and Chinese President Jiang Zemin accepted each other's invitations for summits in Washington and Beijing. The two leaders met in Manila where they are attending the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) conference.

It was another comforting factor in the Hong Kong/China economic and stock market picture, with recent rhetoric about improving Sino/U.S. relations apparently being followed up with actions, Gorges said.
Good relations between China and the United States are crucial for Hong Kong as the two giants are the tiny territory's largest trading partners.
Periods of tension between the two sides, particularly during trade disputes carrying the threat of mutual trade sanctions, have often battered the local bourse.
A senior U.S. official also said Washington felt more work remained before China could join the World Trade Organization.
Gorges said the timing of China's accession to the WTO had been up in the air for a long time.

He noted that U.S. Commerce Secretary Mickey Kantor recently stressed Washington was working hard to help China join the trade body, and added the summits agreement may not have happened if the two sides were seriously at odds over the WTO.
